title: Example Pages: Academic & Blogging
intro: Four ready-made pages you can copy for your own work — a paper summary, a course syllabus, a field-notes blog post and a dataset landing page. Each one is plain JSON in data/pages/.

add_paragraph.heading: How to use them
add_paragraph.text:
Every example is a single file in `data/pages/`. Copy the file, rename it, and edit the words — the layout is already designed. The page opens at `pages/page.html?page=<file name>`, and anywhere else you link to it by name: `@pages.<file name>`.

Nothing here is hard-coded: headings, lists, tables, quotes, notes, links and buttons are all elements, and the order in the file is the order on the page.

add_cards.heading: The four examples
add_cards.intro: Pick the shape closest to what you need, then replace the sample words.

individual_card_details.heading: Paper summary
individual_card_details.text: Explain one paper to a general reader: the question, key findings, a table of the design, a quote, the model, and links to the paper and data.

individual_card_details.heading: Course syllabus
individual_card_details.text: A course at a glance: credits and assessment, learning outcomes, a week-by-week timeline, reading list and an enquiry button.

individual_card_details.heading: Field notes
individual_card_details.text: A diary post with a lead image, a photo gallery, a pull quote and tags — written to be read, not skimmed.

individual_card_details.heading: Dataset release
individual_card_details.text: A landing page for an archive: what is inside, the file table, the citation, limitations and a download link.

add_items_to_list: **Paper summary** — centred opener, tags, key-findings list, table, quote, equation, callout, link rows, two buttons.
**Course syllabus** — at-a-glance table, list, timeline, callout, two more lists, quote and button.
**Blog field notes** — centred opener, lead image, gallery, pull quote, dark callout, tags and button.
**Dataset release** — tags, file table, citation callout, methods and limitations lists, download links.

add_special_note.heading: One rule worth knowing
add_special_note.text: A JSON object can hold each key **once**. If a page needs two headings or three lists, write them in an `add_content_to_page` array — one element per entry — as these examples do. Repeating the same top-level key silently keeps only the last one.
